worldcombat.skill.headbutt.summary: A short, cheap headlong headbutt: low range and a low cooldown, usable at almost any time. A solid hit may leave the target flinched, and striking one that is already reeling hurts more - its value is in sustained pressure.
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.description.0: The headbutt deals about %1$s contact damage with a %2$s block collision radius; the target's defence, type and crits are applied on the hit.
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.description.1: It lunges up to %1$s blocks at %2$s blocks per tick and shoves the target %3$s blocks on a hit.
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.description.2: A solid hit has a %1$s flinch chance for %2$s s; striking a target that is already flinched hits harder.
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.driving.on: Driving form: lunges farther, hits harder and flinches more often, but starts slower and has a longer wind-up and cooldown, and overshoots more easily.
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.driving.off: Quick form: a short, snappy headbutt - faster to cast, steadier footing, slightly lighter.
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.timing: Range %1$s blocks; wind-up %2$s s, recovery %3$s s, costing %5$s PP, cooldown %4$s s from commit.
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.growth.0: From level %1$s the headbutt power rises to %2$s.
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.growth.1: From level %1$s the headbutt power rises to %2$s, the lunge to %3$s blocks and the flinch chance to %4$s.
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.use.0: Keep up close pressure with a low cooldown
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.use.1: Follow up on a target that was just flinched for a harder hit
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.use.2: Nudge a target away from cover at little cost
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.preference.dr: On: lunges farther, hits harder and flinches more often, but starts slower with a longer wind-up and cooldown, and overshoots more easily. Off: a short, snappy headbutt - faster to cast, steadier footing, slightly lighter.
worldcombat.skill.headbutt.preference.ai: Beyond this distance the user closes in first. Larger chases harder and is more likely to stop behind the target after a whiff.

Always: treat it as an ordinary melee move, used whenever possible. Reeling only: only follow up a target that is already flinched (for the higher power); good next to a partner with an opening control move, almost never used on its own.
